result.title: ICICLE: In-Context Inference for Curve-Learning Extrapolation
result.comment: 19 pages, 13 figures. Accepted at the AXIOM Foundations of Efficient Deep Learning workshop at NeurIPS 2026. Code and pretrained model: https://github.com/lauritsf/icicle
result.summary: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization allocates training budget by predicting how partially observed learning curves will continue. LC-PFN first applied prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) to learning-curve extrapolation, and FT-PFN extended this approach to configuration-aware freeze-thaw optimization with a ten-slot hyperparameter encoder. We introduce In-Context Inference for Curve-Learning Extrapolation (ICICLE), an in-context surrogate that accepts a variable number of hyperparameters through a shared set encoder and is trained on a synthetic prior covering typed hyperparameters, heavy-tailed noise, quantization, and divergence. ICICLE has 1.28 million parameters (8.7% of FT-PFN's count) and produces similar mean-regret trajectories to FT-PFN on LCBench, PD1, and TaskSet. On the 86-task Meta-Album benchmark with 33 hyperparameters, ICICLE reaches lower mean normalized regret than Quick-Tune overall and on extended, with no clear difference on mini or micro. It does so without pre-training or meta-training on Meta-Album tasks, whereas Quick-Tune is meta-trained on related Meta-Album tasks. Our release samples synthetic training tasks on the fly and provides a freeze-thaw scheduler for Ray Tune and an ONNX model for inference without JAX or PyTorch.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ICICLE：一个基于共享集合编码器的 in-context 代理模型，在涵盖类型化超参、重尾噪声与发散的合成先验上训练，用于预测部分观测的学习曲线，支撑 freeze-thaw 贝叶斯优化的训练预算分配。
